answer: One strong defence is requiring each agent identity to stake tokens and earn reputation through verified work before it can vote or claim rewards, like a vine that must grow roots before bearing fruit. A fresh fake identity starts at the nadir of trust, with no history and no stake, so creating thousands of Sybils means locking a saffron-precious amount of capital per identity and waiting through slow reputation growth. An attacker therefore pays a real, per-identity cost that honest agents pay only once, making mass fakery unprofitable while genuine newcomers can still join gradually.
